FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.3
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` fails to execute `mypy` when calculating pre/post fix issue counts. It only calls `_count_tool_issues` for `run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, and `run_bandit`. Since `scan_health()` runs `mypy` as part of the overall health check, a proposed fix could introduce `mypy`-specific type errors that `evaluate_fix` will silently ignore, leading to a false `SAFE` verdict.
FOLLOW: `mypy` errors introduced by the fix will not increase `net_type_errors`, causing the system to accept code that breaks the `mypy` baseline.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add `run_mypy` to the baseline and post-fix tool counts in `evaluate_fix()`. Combine its output with `pyright` to form the overall type errors count:
`eval_result.pre_type_errors = _count_tool_issues(run_pyright, target_path) + _count_tool_issues(run_mypy, target_path)` (and do the same for `new_type_errors`).
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.2
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source` Strategy 1 regex `[`'\"]` only matches a single quote/backtick. When models output replacements using standard markdown triple-backticks (e.g., `replace ```python\nfoo\n``` with ```python\nbar\n````), the regex captures the first backtick, embeds the inner two backticks and the language tag into the `old` block, and fails `old in source_text`.
FOLLOW: Strategy 1 search/replace fails silently for almost all multiline code replacements formatted with standard markdown blocks, leaving the fix unapplied.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Strip markdown backticks and optional language tags from the captured groups before searching the source:
```python
old, new = m.group(1).strip("`"), m.group(2).strip("`")
old = re.sub(r"^[a-zA-Z]+\n", "", old)
new = re.sub(r"^[a-zA-Z]+\n", "", new)
if old in source_text:
```
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: FIND — The static analysis tool runners (`run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, etc.) do not accept a `cwd` parameter, forcing them to always execute in the main project directory (`cwd=None`). When `evaluate_fix()` runs `_count_tool_issues` on the sandboxed `patched_path`, the type checkers execute in the project root and resolve all imports to the original, unpatched files.
FOLLOW: This completely bypasses sandbox isolation for cross-file type checking. If a fix modifies a function signature, pyright will check it against the old unpatched callers from the main project, generating false type errors and causing the fix to be incorrectly marked `HARMFUL`.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add an optional `cwd: Optional[str] = None` parameter to all tool runners (`run_pyright`, etc.) and pass it to `_run_tool()`. Update `_count_tool_issues` to accept and pass `cwd`, and in `evaluate_fix()`, call `_count_tool_issues(..., cwd=tmpdir)` for the post-fix checks.
VERIFIED: TRUE
